text:
lee: Quick callout. Found a few parity issues between the Python SDK and the REST API after pairing with a customer onboarding. Putting notes here so we don't lose them.

lee: 1) Embeddings: REST has POST /v1/embeddings/batch which accepts an array of inputs and returns batched vectors. Python SDK only exposes `client.embed()` for a single input (docs example shows list but implementation raises on >1). customer workload needs batch for performance.

lee: repro:
```
# REST (works)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings/batch \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"embed-small","inputs":["a","b","c"]}'

# Python SDK (raises)
vectors = client.embeddings.create(model='embed-small', input=['a','b','c'])
# -> ValueError: "input must be a single string" (0.10.1)
```

lee: 2) Streaming param name mismatch: REST uses `stream=true`, Python SDK method `client.generate(..., stream=True)` works, but the TypeScript/Go SDKs use `enable_streaming` and the REST docs have `stream`. This inconsistency caused our sample app templates to fail across SDKs.

juan: which python package version? we've had a split between the thin wrapper and the generated client code.

lee: python 0.10.1 pinned in the onboarding repo. I inspected the SDK code and saw an input validation shim that normalizes singletons but forbids lists. looks like the generator didn't include the batch endpoint.

marie: thanks. we should treat batch embeddings as a missing endpoint (not just a param drift). Can you attach the failing stacktrace? Also add the sample app that broke so devex can update quickstarts.

lee: stacktrace (short): "ValueError: embeddings input must be a single string\n at client.embeddings.create(...)". repro repo: https://git.redwood.internal/lee/embeds-batch-repro (private).

sam: adding infra nuance: we also saw SDK backoff defaults differ. REST SDK callers benefit from gateway backoffs on 429; python sdk retries are aggressive (no jitter) and hit 429 -> thrown. customer noticed higher error rate in bulk ingestion.

lee: exact example: hitting /v1/embeddings/batch via REST gets `429 Retry-After: 2` and client retries -> success. python sdk returns 429 error to user (no retry).

juan: is this a policy difference or missing header propagation? sometimes our generated clients swallow `Retry-After` and map to exceptions without exposing headers.

sam: i can confirm the python http layer sets max_retries=0 by default in the transport wrapper (legacy). there's an open item to standardize retry config across SDKs. I'll PR a patch to: preserve Retry-After, enable exponential backoff with jitter by default, and surface retry hooks.

marie: OK action items: 1) add batch embeddings endpoint to python SDK surface (juan), 2) unify streaming param names across SDKs (devex + SDK owners), 3) standardize retry/backoff defaults and preserve Retry-After header (sam), 4) add quickstart sample app updates and note migration steps (devex).

ci-bot: Created issue RED-3790: "Python SDK: add embeddings batch endpoint, align retry behavior with gateway, fix param naming parity" assigned to juan and sam.

lee: thanks. small UX note: sample app failure was confusing because the error message said "use a single string" but the REST docs and quickstart show passing a list. might be worth adding a deprecation warning or compatibility shim in the SDK for one release.

juan: will add a compatibility shim + failing test to the python client test suite so we don't regress. I'll also update the changelog with a migration note.

sam: i will prototype retry defaults and add an integration test that mocks Retry-After. will coordinate with infra to ensure gateway headers aren't being filtered by our proxies.

marie: thanks all. once PRs are up tag me and i'll schedule a quick review slot. we should aim to include this in the next patch release (0.10.2).

lee: great. i'll update the onboarding repo to point to the repro and include a short note in the onboarding checklist to pin a fixed sdk version until the patch lands.

juan: noted. leaving this thread, will link PRs here.

lee: closing for now, will reopen if new regressions appear."
